title: Anonymous barcode rendering can allocate oversized ZXing BitMatrix/BufferedImage from attacker-controlled text
source: anonymous query parameters t and w
sink: BarCodeSupport.createBarCodeImage computes Code128 auto width from new Code128Writer().encode(content).length and then calls MultiFormatWriter.encode, followed by MatrixToImageWriter.toBufferedImage
driver: attacker-controlled content length and height parameter; width is recomputed from encoded content length after the fixed 1200 width cap, so long t can drive large matrix/image allocation
retention: request-burst allocation during ZXing encoding and PNG rendering; failure can occur before normal response cleanup
bound: Endpoint is anonymous by isIgnoreAuth. application.yml only sets max-http-header-size 32KB; no app-level t length cap or barcode CPU/heap guard found. QR format has capacity exceptions, but Code128 path remains a strong allocation candidate.
impact: Static evidence for a default anonymous non-disk request-burst DoS candidate. Needs dynamic probe to confirm exact payload threshold under default Tomcat request-line/header limits and JVM heap.
dynamic_probe: Run default service with bounded heap. Request /commons/barcode/render with increasing t length and w=1200, prefer CODE_128/default format. Monitor heap, allocation failure, GC death, latency, 5xx, and process health. Stop before host pressure; success requires OOM/GC death/restart or sustained HTTP unavailability.
